title: The dumb ox
hookLine: Thomas Aquinas was so quiet at school they called him the dumb ox
tomorrow: Aquinas: it all seems like straw

lines: THEY CALL HIM THE DUMB OX.
cards: In a lecture hall in Cologne sits a big student who almost never speaks. He listens, he writes, he doesn't argue in class. The other students decide he can't be very bright, and they give him a nickname: the dumb ox.

One classmate feels sorry for him and offers to go over the lessons with him. The big student says yes, thank you, and sits while the classmate explains. Then the classmate gets tangled in a hard passage.
And the quiet one, gently, explains the whole thing, clearly, start to finish. The student is Thomas Aquinas.

teach.h: HIS FAMILY TRIED TO STOP HIM.
teach.b: Thomas had already paid a price to be in that room.

His noble Italian family had other plans for him, and when he joined Dominic's preachers, the friars from two days ago, his family stopped him on the road and kept him at home for a long time, trying to change his mind.
They couldn't. Now here he is in Cologne, studying under a well-known teacher, Albert, later called Albert the Great. What happened next comes from Thomas's early biographer, William of Tocco.
Albert gives the class a hard question and has Thomas answer it in public.
He does, so clearly that Albert turns to the room: you call him the dumb ox, but this ox will one day bellow so loud the whole world will hear. Notice what the quiet was. Not emptiness: attention.
He wasn't speaking because he was listening, all the way down. And notice how he took the classmate's offer: no correction, no showing off, just yes, thank you.

teach.h: SWIFT TO HEAR, SLOW TO SPEAK.
teach.b: The letter of James puts it plainly, in the King James Bible: "let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak." Later Thomas would write a great deal, and Christians still read him, argue with him and learn from him.
But it started with a young man nobody thought much of, sitting in the back, listening. The loudest voice in the room isn't always the one that understands.

how: Catholics honor Thomas Aquinas as a saint and a Doctor of the Church, and his writings are studied in Catholic seminaries and universities and by readers of other churches too.

o: a farm animal in one of Jesus's parables
a nickname for quiet Thomas, who was listening
an insult for a monk who refused to study

s: Thomas was called the dumb ox because he failed his classes
he was quiet, so classmates assumed he wasn't bright. he understood more than they did.
Thomas accepted a classmate's offer to explain the lessons
he said yes, thank you, and then explained the hard passage himself when the classmate got stuck.
Thomas's family was glad he joined the Dominicans
they stopped him on the road and kept him at home for a long time.

games.q: you're Thomas, the quiet student. a classmate who thinks you're slow offers to explain the lessons to you. what do you do?
o: tell him you already understand them.
say yes, thank you, and listen.
games.why: he says yes and listens. when the classmate gets stuck, Thomas gently explains it all.

practice: Bring to mind someone in your life who doesn't say much, at work, at the table, in a group chat where they only ever send a thumbs up.
Wonder for a moment what they notice that the rest of you miss, and what they've never been asked. If you pray, give thanks for them; if not, let your respect for them grow a little.

wordCard.voice: Dumb ox. The nickname classmates gave Thomas Aquinas because he was quiet. His teacher Albert said the ox would one day bellow.

carryVoice: Your line: the ox will bellow. Quiet is not the same as empty. Day eight hundred twenty-one.
